query: What does the EndoSLAM dataset contain, and how many ex-vivo sub-datasets are provided for each organ group?
reference_answer: EndoSLAM combines 3D point clouds, capsule and standard endoscopy recordings, synthetic data, and a clinically used colonoscope recording with CT ground truth. Its ex-vivo portion has 35 sub-datasets with 6D pose ground truth: 18 colon, 12 stomach, and 5 small-intestine sub-datasets.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we introduce a comprehensive endoscopic SLAM dataset consisting of 3D point cloud data for six porcine organs, capsule and standard endoscopy recordings, synthetically generated data as well as clinically in use conventional endoscope recording of the phantom colon with computed tomography(CT) scan ground truth.
In total, 35 sub-datasets are provided with 6D pose ground truth for the ex-vivo part: 18 sub-datasets for colon, 12 sub-datasets for stomach, and 5 subdatasets for small intestine

query: What design requirements does EndoSLAM target for endoscopic SLAM research?
reference_answer: The requirements include time-synchronized 6-DoF pose ground truth, high-precision 3D reconstructions, multiple organs and individuals, varied camera intrinsics, frame rates, viewing angles and lighting, and diagnostically meaningful features such as polyps.

evidence.quote: The dataset is recorded using multiple endoscope cameras and ex-vivo porcine GI organs belonging to different animals and is designed to meet the following major requirements for scientific research and development of endoscopic SLAM methods:
Time-synchronized, ground-truth 6 DoF pose data
High precision, ground-truth 3D reconstructions
Multiple organs from multiple individuals
Images from cameras with varying intrinsic properties
Image sequences with differing native frame rates
Images acquired from different camera view angle such as perpendicular, vertical and tubular
Images under a variety of lighting conditions
Distinguishable features of diagnostic significance (e.g. presence/absence of polyps).

query: How are the ex-vivo frames distributed across cameras, and how are pose coordinates represented?
reference_answer: The ex-vivo set has 42,700 frames: 21,428 HighCam, 17,978 LowCam, 239 PillCam, and 3,055 MiroCam images. Each pose has quaternion orientation (x, y, z, w) and absolute position (x, y, z) in meters.

evidence.quote: The ex-vivo part of the dataset consists of a total of 42,700 frames. Of these, 21,428 images are from the HighCam, 17,978 images are from the LowCam, 239 images are from the PillCam and 3055 images are from the MiroCam.

Trajectories for each organ can be found in the folder Poses in (.csv) and (.txt) format with 6D pose coordinates: four orientation parameters (x; y; z; w) in quaternions and three absolute position parameters (x; y; z) in meters.

query: How is camera motion ground truth obtained in the EndoSLAM setup?
reference_answer: A 7-DoF Franka Emika Panda arm stabilizes the camera trajectory and records ground-truth motion poses. It is hand-guided and records poses at 1 kHz, with 0.1 mm repeatability precision.

evidence.quote: Franka Emika Panda robotic arm with 7 degree of freedom and 0.1mm pose repeatability precision is utilized to provide trajectory stabilization and ground-truth pose recording of the camera motions.
The robot controls the motion of the cameras in handguided mode and supplies pose recording at high-frequency, 1 kHz (see Fig. A.1 a).

query: What clinical-system validation experiment was added to EndoSLAM?
reference_answer: The authors recorded 12,250 RGB frames while advancing and withdrawing an Olympus CFHQ-190L colonoscope through a lubricated silicone colon phantom. A Canon Aquilion Precision CT scanner supplied the phantom’s 3D ground truth.

evidence.quote: A video sequence consisting of 12,250 RGB frames of a silicone phantom (Colonoscopy Trainer, #2003, the Chamberlain Group) were captured using the scope, video processor (CV-190), and the CV-190L light source.
A ground truth 3D model of the silicone phantom was captured using a Canon Aquilion Precision CT scanner.

query: Which image transformations are provided for robustness studies in the dataset?
reference_answer: The augmentation functions include resizing, Gaussian blur, fish-eye distortion, depth-of-field simulation through shift-variant defocus blur, and frame-rate variation.

evidence.quote: The transformations include resizing, Gaussian blur, fish-eye distortion, depth-of-field simulation via shift-variant defocus blurring, and frame-rate variation.

query: What synthetic data does EndoSLAM provide, and what annotations does it include?
reference_answer: The VRCaps simulation uses CT DICOM topography and RGB endoscopic textures with cinematic rendering. It provides 21,887 colon frames, 12,558 small-intestine frames, and 1,548 stomach frames at 320x320 resolution, with positional and pixel-wise depth ground truth.

evidence.quote: The platform was built with the use of real computed tomography (CT) images in DICOM format for topography and endoscopic images in RGB format for texture assignment.
we have recorded three sample endoscopic videos that containing 21,887 frames from colon, 12,558 frames from small intestine, and 1548 frames from stomach
having both positional and pixel-wise depth ground truth.

query: What problems does Endo-SfMLearner address in endoscopic monocular estimation, and how?
reference_answer: It addresses brightness changes, shallow-depth-of-field/non-Lambertian effects, and scale inconsistency between frames. It aligns brightness during training, weights photometric loss by brightness/depth consistency, and adds geometry-consistency loss so depth and relative poses remain scale-consistent.

evidence.quote: static scene assumption, scale ambiguity between consecutive frames, brightness variety which basically stems from shallow depth-of-field and the organ tissues exhibiting non-lambertian surface property which are non-diffusely reflecting light particles make it difficult to provide both locally and globally consistent trajectory estimations.

Our method proposes two solutions to the light source rooted problems in depth and pose estimation. First proposed solution is to equate brightness conditions throughout the training and validation sets with brightness transformation function and the other is to weight the photometric loss with the brightness coefficient to punish the depth estimation with higher cost under different enlightenment conditions.
We are using geometry consistency loss for scale-inconsistency between consecutive frames caused by alternating distances between the camera and organ tissue.

query: What are the roles of DispNet and Attention PoseNet in Endo-SfMLearner?
reference_answer: DispNet takes one image and predicts its disparity map using an encoder-decoder with ResNet blocks and skip connections. Attention PoseNet takes a consecutive image pair and predicts relative 6-DoF pose; its encoder inserts the ESAB spatial-attention block between ReLU and max pooling.

evidence.quote: The depth network which consists of encoder and decoder parts takes single image I i as input and gives output the corresponding disparity map D i .
The pose network takes the consecutive image tuples (I i , I i +1 ) as input by superposing and outputs the relative 6-DoF pose, P i,i +1 .
We have integrated attention module to the encoder of PoseNet between ReLU and maxpooling layers.

query: How does the Endo-SfMLearner spatial attention block (ESAB) operate?
reference_answer: ESAB computes non-local pixel relations with convolutions and dot products, applies ReLU and softmax-based weighting, upsamples the resulting attention map, and adds it to the input through a residual connection.

evidence.quote: The ESAB mechanism is non-local convolutional process.
The dot product, θ(X ) ϕ(X ) ⊤ , gives a measurement for the input covariance, which can be defined as a degree of tendency between two feature maps at different channels.
Short connection between the input X and the output F finalizes the block operations for the residual learning.

query: What losses make up the Endo-SfMLearner objective, and how is illumination handled?
reference_answer: The objective is a weighted sum of brightness-aware photometric, smoothness, and geometry-consistency losses. Illumination is handled by an affine brightness transformation of the synthesized frame before photometric comparison; depth inconsistency also weights the photometric loss.

evidence.quote: We are using three loss functions to guide the network without labels; brightness-aware photometric loss, smoothness loss, and geometry consistency loss.
The overall objective of the system is to minimize the weighted sum of brightness-aware photometric loss
Endo-SfMLearner network predicts a brightness transformation parameter set which tries to align the brightness of input images during training on the fly and in a self-supervised manner.
brightness-aware photometric loss is weighted with higher constant if the predicted and interpolated depth maps are inconsistent for each pixel.

query: How are ATE and relative pose error defined in the evaluation?
reference_answer: ATE measures global trajectory consistency after best rigid alignment and uses the translational difference at each pose; the overall ATE is the trajectory-wide RMS. Relative pose error measures pose-change differences over a fixed interval, with separate translational and rotational errors, reported here for interval 1.

evidence.quote: The ATE is a measure of global consistency between two trajectories, comparing absolute distances between ground truth and predicted poses at each point in time.
The overall error throughout trajectory is defined by the root mean square of ATE i .
Relative pose error measures the difference in the change in pose over a fixed length Delta1between two trajectories.
The errors are reported for Delta1equals to 1.

query: What training protocol was used for the pose-estimation comparison?
reference_answer: All methods used the same data and parameters: 2,039 Unity colon training images and 509 validation images, 200 epochs, shuffled batches of four, ADAM with initial learning rate 10^-4, and validation after every epoch.

evidence.quote: All methods including Endo-SfMLearner are trained with the same data and parameter set for the sake of fairness and unbiased results.
The training and validation dataset consist of 2039 and 509 colon images generated in the Unity simulation environment, respectively.
We train all networks in 200 epochs with randomly shuffled batches each size of 4 images, optimize by ADAM with an initial learning rate 10 -4 and validate after each epoch.

query: What do the ablation results show about ESAB and the brightness-aware loss?
reference_answer: Table 2 shows that adding ESAB and brightness-aware photometric loss reduces rotational errors relative to the SC-SfMLearner baseline in most tests. The ablation analysis also reports that ESAB improves texture awareness and brightness-aware loss improves sensitivity to illumination; together they produce the best performance.

evidence.quote: We observed a considerable decrease in rotational errors for Endo-SfMLearner with respect to the baseline method, SC-SfMLearner, which proves the effectiveness of spatial attention block integrated to pose network encoder and brightness-aware photometric loss.
The attention module makes Endo-SfMLearner more responsive for depth alterations on the synthetically generated images of all organs.

Ablation studies clarify that the attention block provides the awareness for the edges and texture details and brightness aware loss increases the sensitivity of depth estimation for illumination changes.

query: How does Endo-SfMLearner behave on sharp turns and fish-eye camera data in Figure 5?
reference_answer: On sharp corners, Endo-SfMLearner is more accurate than SC-SfMLearner in translational and rotational errors and preserves scale consistency. The MiroCam trajectory tests robustness to high fish-eye lens distortion; overall Endo-SfMLearner follows ground truth better than the other models.

evidence.quote: At those points, EndoSfMLearner yields performance with higher accuracy compared to SC-SfMLearner not just qualitatively but also quantitatively in terms of both translational, and rotational errors.
It illustrates the case where SC-SfMLearner loose the scale consistency after sharp corner angle which is not the case for Endo-SfMLearner.
MiroCam exhibits fish-eye camera properties with high lens distortion.

It is seen that the Endo-SfMLearner outputs generally follow the shape of the ground truth, specifically, it catches rotations more consistently which is the main reason for the decrease in rotational relative pose error.

query: What quantitative depth-estimation results are reported across organs?
reference_answer: Using RMSE, Endo-SfMLearner is evaluated on 1,548 stomach, 1,257 small-intestine, and 1,062 colon frames. Although trained on synthetic colon frames, it achieves mean RMSE 0.2966 on stomach and 0.1785 on small intestine, with errors decreasing for regions farther than 14 mm.

evidence.quote: The results are evaluated in terms of root mean square error (RMSE) on 1548 stomach, 1257 small intestine, and 1062 colon frames.
Even if the training and validation dataset consist of synthetic colon frames, Endo-SfMLearner depicts high performance on stomach and small intestine with 0.2966 and 0.1785 mean RMSE.
Endo-SfMLearner is able to estimate the relatively far regions more accurately than the remaining ones, although it is optimized for the images obtained by shallow Depth of Field cameras.

query: What does the qualitative depth evaluation show about polyps, reflections, blur, and distortion?
reference_answer: The method detects polyp boundaries and details, stays more consistent in reflective regions because of brightness-aware loss, and remains usable under camera variation. Increasing fish-eye distortion makes central pixels appear closer, whereas stronger Gaussian blur generally makes all models predict longer distances.

evidence.quote: Fig. 7 b indicates that the method successfully detects the boundaries and details of polyps.

the propounded method generates more consistent depth maps for the pixels where the light reflections occur thanks to the robustness against illumination changes provided by brightness-aware photometric loss.
In Fig. 7 d, it can be observed that the center of frames are predicted as closer to the camera with an increase of distortion level.
the general tendency for all models is to make longer distance predictions with the increase of the Gaussian Blur effect.

query: What is the 3D reconstruction pipeline and how accurate is it on the four evaluated trajectories?
reference_answer: The pipeline detects and suppresses reflections, stitches frames with SIFT/RANSAC, estimates depth with Tsai-Shah shape from shading, aligns to scans with ICP, and computes cloud-to-mesh RMSE. Reported RMSEs are 0.65 cm (Colon-IV), 0.54 cm (Small Intestine), 0.73 cm (Stomach-III), and 1.38 cm (Phantom Colon).

evidence.quote: The steps of the procedure can be summarized under four fundamental techniques which are Otsu threshold-based reflection detection, OPENCV inpainting-based reflection suppression, feature matching and tracking based image stitching and nonlambertion surface reconstruction.
To establish feature point correspondences between frames, SIFT feature matching and RANSAC based pair elimination are employed ( Brown and Lowe, 2007 ).
Using that pipeline, RMSEs of 0.65 cm, 0.54 cm, 0.73 cm, and 1.38 cm are obtained for ColonIV, Small Intestine, Stomach-III, and Phantom Colon trajectories, respectively.
Iterative Closest Point(ICP) was used to align the ground truth data and reconstructed surface after manually labeling a common line segment.

query: What limitations and future directions do the authors identify?
reference_answer: The ex-vivo setup differs from real endoscopy because organs are cleaned and fixed to scaffolds, so muscle contractions, fecal matter, and fluid effects are absent. Future work will broaden the dataset to other visualization modalities, improve data adaptability, and combine Endo-SfMLearner with segmentation, abnormality detection, and classification in multi-task/meta-learning.

evidence.quote: Since the tissues are cleaned and stabilized to the scaffold, the provided ex-vivo setup differs from the real endoscopy procedure in terms of the movement stem from the contraction of muscles as well as fecal matter and fluid rooted vision problems.
Our future work will focus on generalizing the EndoSLAM dataset concept to other visualization techniques and create datasets with various other imaging modalities.
Furthermore, we aim to examine and improve the data adaptability of the Endo-SfMLearner and address these issues as next steps.
we plan to investigate the combination of EndoSfmLearner with segmentation, abnormality detection, and classification tasks in the concept of multi-task and meta-learning

query: What does the appendix report about pose estimation on synthetic Unity trajectories?
reference_answer: Synthetic Unity trajectories are easier to follow, so all methods improve. SC-SfMLearner and Endo-SfMLearner track them more accurately because of geometry consistency, and Endo-SfMLearner has the lowest mean ATE; lower rotational error from Monodepth2 or SfMLearner is not treated as overall superiority because Unity rotations stay near the identity matrix.

evidence.quote: On the contrary to real ex-vivo records, synthetically generated trajectories are more straightforward and easier to follow.
For all synthetically generated trajectories, EndoSfMLearner exhibits lowest mean absolute trajectory error(ATE).

Since the rotations cannot be changed frequently and easily while recording clear images in Unity environment, they remain close to identity matrix which is generally predicted by Monodepth2 and SfMLearner.
